summary: AstroPulse is a real-time astronaut health monitoring and autonomous medical triage platform built for deep-space missions where communication delays prevent immediate guidance from Earth. Aligned with NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight, AstroPulse streams physiological and spacesuit telemetry—including heart rate, arterial oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, core temperature, xEMU suit pressure, inspired pCO₂, and radiation dosimetry—via FastAPI and WebSockets into an interactive Next.js mission control dashboard. Crew members can inspect clickable anatomical and spacesuit nodes on a Holographic Diagnostic Map, log daily sleep hours, blood glucose, mood, and symptoms through a self-assessment module, and read plain-language explanations for every vital sign. When anomalies occur, an onboard AI Flight Surgeon powered by Groq LLaMA 3 delivers instant clinical triage and step-by-step stabilization countermeasures, empowering astronauts to detect, understand, and act on physical and behavioral health risks independently.
details:
What Does AstroPulse Do & How Does It Work?

AstroPulse is an end-to-end astronaut health monitoring, self-assessment, and autonomous medical triage platform designed for lunar, deep-space, and planetary surface missions. A Python FastAPI backend ingests and streams multi-crew physiological and spacesuit telemetry over secure WebSockets (WSS) with automatic heartbeat keep-alive to a Next.js and TypeScript Mission Control interface.

Astronauts can monitor live vital signs (heart rate via ECG Lead II, arterial SpO₂, systolic/diastolic blood pressure, core body temperature, xEMU suit pressure in psid, inspired pCO₂ in mmHg, and cumulative radiation dosimetry in mSv) across seven specialized operational modules: Mission Overview, Crew Monitoring, Health Analytics, AI Flight Surgeon, Alert Center, Radiation Monitoring, and System Settings.

How It Addresses NASA's Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight

1. Space Radiation: Tracks solar particle event (SPE) proton flux, galactic cosmic ray (GCR) baselines, and 24-hour cumulative crew dosimetry (mSv), triggering EVA abort and ALARA water-wall shielding protocols before exposure limits are breached.

2. Isolation and Confinement: Includes an interactive Astronaut Daily Self-Assessment module where crew members log daily sleep hours, blood glucose (mg/dL), mood/behavioral state (1–5), and symptom notes, receiving immediate preventive behavioral and circadian guidance.

3. Distance from Earth: Solves deep-space communication latency (where Earth-to-Mars signals take up to 22 minutes one way) using an onboard AI Flight Surgeon powered by Groq LLaMA 3 that generates real-time clinical triage and step-by-step stabilization procedures locally.

4. Gravity Fields: Evaluates microgravity-induced cephalad fluid shifts, cardiovascular deconditioning, and neuro-vestibular adaptation through anatomical telemetry nodes and blood pressure/heart rate trend analysis.

5. Hostile/Closed Environments: Monitors closed-loop life support parameters including xEMU suit differential pressure, Rapid Cycle Amine (RCA) CO₂ scrubber load (inspired pCO₂), and Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) thermal regulation.

Benefits, Intended Impact & Human-Centered Factors

Not every crew member on a mission is a flight surgeon. AstroPulse pairs color-coded status indicators (Nominal, Caution, Critical) and pulsing sidebar operation alerts with plain-language explanations under every vital sign explaining how the measurement works and why it matters in space. When a critical anomaly triggers, crew members can inspect the exact affected anatomical region or suit subsystem on an interactive Holographic Diagnostic Map and execute guided stabilization actions immediately.

Tools, Coding Languages & Architecture

- Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (hosted on Vercel)

- Backend & Telemetry Streaming: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, WebSockets (hosted on Render)

- Autonomous Triage AI: Groq Cloud API running LLaMA 3

- Version Control & Collaboration: Git and GitHub (https://github.com/BenjaminJKHong/astro_hope_2026)

Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Usage Disclosure

AstroPulse integrates Groq LLaMA 3 within the AI Flight Surgeon module to synthesize live biometric anomalies into structured clinical triage recommendations and stabilization checklists. Super Intelligence (SI) coding and generative tools were also used during hackathon development to assist with TypeScript/Python boilerplate, UI prototyping, and team emblem artwork. No NASA logos, flags, or official mission insignia were generated or modified using SI tools.
